acceptance: The owner approved a written design recorded on this item.
A registry scale-list edit can no longer change a committed bundle's class without a visible failure.
context: Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).
description:
## Problem
Since #4304 a bundle's effective compliance class is derived at read time from the current registry (`subscale_policy.effective_compliance_class`, used by the bundle validator and `results-data/validate_corpus.py`). Editing a benchmark's standard or official scale list therefore reclassifies every stored bundle at the affected scales, including ones stamped official; #4335 showed this for TPC-DS 10000 and above (latent: the corpus has none).

## Change
Design first: either bind classification to the scale list in force when the bundle was produced (recorded in the bundle or by version), or add a check that fails when a registry change alters the class of any committed bundle. Implement only the approved design.

## Decision gates
Stop after the written design (options, effect on the 503 committed bundles, migration) and get the owner's approval. No implementation before that.

## Verification rubric
Pass: a test changes a scale list and shows either that stored bundles keep their class or that the change is refused with the affected bundle ids; corpus validation counts on develop are unchanged.

## Guardrails
- Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed.
- The implementer never resolves review threads on its own pull request; the reviewer or the owner does.
- No polling loop around `make pr-arm`, no `--no-verify`, and no stand-in review unless the owner names the PR and head unprompted.
- Heavy work runs only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking entry point.
- Status reports state only what merged and what was verified, with the evidence.
